clue.text: Great scholar of arithmetic is retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the phrase for arithmetic being is read backwards

parts.note: arithmetic is sums, simple calculations
with the plural sums the verb is becomes are

explanation.surface: A learned man boasts of a numerate scholar who is shy and withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arithmetic is' must be read as the plural 'sums are' before 'retiring' turns the whole of SUMSARE around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch humanist of Rotterdam was one of the greatest Renaissance scholars.

clue.text: Articulate letters from unfaithful lover initially bringing comfort

indicators.note: to articulate is to pronounce, so the letters are spoken

parts.note: the plural of the letter E is Es

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Clearly expressed letters from a cheating partner, oddly comforting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' are Es, said aloud as EASE; F, U, L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Easeful is a poetic adjective meaning soothing or giving relief, as in Keats's easeful death.

clue.text: Nothing stops ardent romance

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the nothing word blocks the middle of ardent

parts.note: afire means burning, ardent
FA, short for 'sweet FA' (sweet Fanny Adams), is British slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing can put an end to passionate love.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is a British slang phrase meaning nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-flavoured word names a love affair, a romance.

clue.text: Ways of life further south

parts.note: more means further, additional

explanation.surface: Customs and lifestyles found further to the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and conventions of a community, its ways of living.

clue.text: Bernie shortly hosting function in Atlantic City

indicators.note: hosting means holding inside, so the trimmed name goes round the function
shortly means the surname is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Bernie Sanders is the US senator
tan, tangent, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Bernie Sanders, briefly, holds an event in Atlantic City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Atlantic' is a link, placing the city on Spain's Atlantic coast; 'Atlantic City' is the New Jersey misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Santander is a port city in northern Spain, also known for its bank.

clue.text: Nietzsche reticently welcoming dissident

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the answer sits inside the phrase Nietzsche reticently

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: The outspoken philosopher, uncharacteristically quiet, takes in a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views at odds with an established doctrine, a dissenter from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Epic poet, big hit in America

definitions.meaning: the Greek poet credited with the Iliad and Odyssey
in baseball a home run is called by this nickname

explanation.surface: An epic poet becomes a smash success in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The bard of ancient Greece shares his name with American slang for a home run.

clue.text: Arguing violently about a drug, drops measuring equipment

indicators.note: violently suggests something tossed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A heated row over a drug leads someone to drop measuring equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb; it is raindrops, part of the definition. 'about' places A and E around the jumbled ARGUING.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain gauge is an instrument measuring rainfall, the drops collected in a set time.

clue.text: Educated workers with books about leftist

parts.note: TU, a trade union, is an organisation of workers

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the books are reversed

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: Workers with leftist reading matter got their education.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutored means taught privately, a past-participle synonym of educated.

clue.text: Censure Conservative Party over end of compassion

parts.note: Dem is short for Democrat, a party

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of compassion

explanation.surface: A politician criticises the Tory party for its lack of compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the pieces one above the next in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn is to censure, to express strong disapproval.

clue.text: Stigmas and timeless indignity attached to homelessness, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of homelessness
less the time abbreviation T, so the synonym for indignity loses that letter

parts.note: an affront is an insult or indignity

explanation.surface: A sociological sentence about the shame and humiliation attached to being without a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stigmas' looks like social disgrace, matching 'indignity', but it is the botanical sense. 'timeless' removes T from AFFRONT, and S, the end of homelessness, is attached in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice is the dried stigmas of the saffron crocus flower, the parts that catch pollen.

clue.text: Slightly wet, Maureen is figure on the left

parts.note: Mo is a pet form of the name Maureen
ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: Maureen, a little damp, poses as a figure standing on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the left' just places the pieces; the figure is TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something lightly is to make it slightly wet, a verb sense.

clue.text: It's only just light and RAF is on manoeuvres

parts.note: fair can mean light in colour, as of hair or skin

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters of RAF and is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A report that the air force is out on exercises at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'barely', but 'only just' here means 'only fair', the idiom of equity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when an outcome is reasonable and equitable, only just in the sense of only right.

clue.text: Defender of England, not Europe? Get stuffed!

indicators.note: not says one letter is left out of the saint's name

parts.note: St George is England's patron saint, its legendary defender against the dragon

explanation.surface: A rude Eurosceptic retort from a defender of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuffed!' sounds like an insult but is read as an order to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat greedily until full, so the imperative is a command to cram oneself with food.

clue.text: Superior pork pie and case of Grenache

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, a fib

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A posh lunch order of a pork pie with a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is British rhyming slang (pork pie, lie), often shortened to 'porky'.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal terms a liege lord is the superior to whom a vassal owes allegiance.

clue.text: Internal examination of huge parrot after death

indicators.note: after sends the huge-and-parrot pieces second, behind the word for death

parts.note: end can mean death
OS, outsize, means huge
to parrot is to copy

explanation.surface: A vet investigates an enormous parrot after it dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge' is not a size word here but the clothing abbreviation OS, outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: An endoscopy uses a camera tube to look inside the body, an internal medical examination.

clue.text: Rubens did work for free

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or knead it, so the letters of Rubens did are reworked

explanation.surface: The painter Rubens produced something without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges RUBENS DID.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburden is to free someone of a load or worry, a verb meaning relieve.

clue.text: Wrongly say I exult in carnal desires

indicators.note: wrongly means in the wrong order, so the letters of say I exult are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: I mistakenly rejoice in lustful pleasures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexuality covers a person's sexual feelings and desires.

clue.text: Eric heartily cross after relative loses last big race

indicators.note: the final letter of the relative is dropped

parts.note: a grandpa is a relative

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: X is a cross

explanation.surface: Eric is very angry after his grandfather loses the last big race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like Eric's mood but stands for the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand prix is a major motor-racing event in the Formula One championship.

clue.text: Gutless gangster mugs shoppers

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: mugs and asses both mean fools

explanation.surface: A cowardly gangster robs shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to shop someone is to inform on them, and a grass is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers here are informers who betray criminals to the police.

clue.text: Half of banana spread over corset of escort, perhaps

indicators.note: the second half of banana is used
in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the spread is reversed

parts.note: marg, margarine, is a spread

explanation.surface: A recipe of half a banana smeared over a corset belonging to an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corset' rearranges to 'escort', so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of escort gives corset, so it is a word made by that process.

clue.text: Member of crowd texts Mrs May after banks fail

indicators.note: the banks of each word are its outer letters; with them gone only the insides remain

explanation.surface: Someone in a crowd sends messages to Theresa May, the former British prime minister, after a banking collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the edges of three words: EXT, R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: In films an extra is a non-speaking performer, one of the crowd in a scene.

clue.text: Proposition from Mike after love-filled word of comfort

indicators.note: after sends Mike to the end, behind the filled comforting word
filled means the comforting word has the love letter put inside

parts.note: there, as in 'there, there', is said to comfort someone
love is zero in tennis, O
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A suggestion from Mike after soothing words full of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love-filled' reads as an adjective, but it says the love letter fills the comforting word.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition proved from axioms.

clue.text: Crafty type taking money from supporter

indicators.note: taking from means removing, so the money letter is taken away

parts.note: a partisan is a committed supporter
P, penny, stands for money

explanation.surface: A cunning character takes cash from a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' suggests cunning but means skilled in a craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled craftsperson, literally a crafty type.

clue.text: Gather together in the morning, when heading to school

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pupils gather together in the morning on their way to school.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity, a synonym of gather.

clue.text: Good people conserving energy, following cruel benefits assessment

parts.note: mean can mean unkind or cruel

indicators.note: conserving means keeping inside, so the saints hold the energy letter

parts.note: saints are good people, each abbreviated ST
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A political complaint that a cruel benefits test is being run by worthy people.
explanation.walkthrough: Saints are a standard pair for 'good people': each is abbreviated ST, so two of them hold the energy letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British welfare a means test checks a claimant's income before state support is paid.

clue.text: Considered emus edible, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether emus are good to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mused means pondered or reflected, a past-tense synonym of considered.

clue.text: Farmhand and pig on edges of Exmoor

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A farm worker and a pig on the fringes of Exmoor, a moorland in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sower is someone who sows seed, a farm worker.

clue.text: Earnest and oddly sweary notes from short people

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of sweary

parts.note: people short of money write IOUs, notes promising payment

explanation.surface: A sincere complaint about foul-mouthed notes from people of small stature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short people' suggests height; here they are short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious and earnest both describe someone sincere and grave, not joking.

clue.text: Moderates finally dragged Italy back towards the centre

indicators.note: back means the joined letters are read in reverse
finally takes the last letter of Moderates

parts.note: drawn means pulled or dragged
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Political moderates have pulled Italy back to the political centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SDRAWNI around.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwards means moving toward the inside or middle of something, an adverb of direction.

clue.text: South American dictionary describing unknown dog

indicators.note: describing is read as drawing around, so the dictionary goes round the unknown

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A South American reference book describes a mysterious canine breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' in the geometric sense of drawing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian spitz breed of dog.

clue.text: Arachne interrupts randy, riotous railway workers

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the setter sits inside the jumbled letters
riotous means wild and unruly, so the letters of randy are rearranged

parts.note: Arachne is the setter, who refers to herself as me

explanation.surface: The setter breaks into a lusty, rowdy crowd of railwaymen.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so Arachne gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardmen work in railway yards, sorting and coupling wagons.
